about_the_game:
Tabletop Fantasy War is a turn-based strategy game set in the fantasy world of Korsak, a world entirely created by a child while developing his dream tabletop game.

Inspired by classic tabletop games, in Tabletop Fantasy War, the first step is to create and customize your unit groups in the unit hall. You can choose between two distinct factions. Each faction has units with different abilities and stats, and an entirely different research tree. After configuring your unit groups, you can start a match.

In the Tabletop Fantasy War demo, you'll be able to play skirmishes against the computer or other players in split-screen, and online multiplayer matches. We have two servers for online mode, one located in Europe (Amsterdam) and the other in North America (New York). Matches are played on relatively small maps for a maximum of 2 to 3 players. There are three maps available, set in different areas of the world of Korsak. When you create a game, you decide the amount of points each player will have for deploying unit groups. Each unit group has a cost that depends on the units that compose it. Once all players have deployed their groups, the game can begin. When the game starts, the positions and all information about all players' groups on the map are revealed. You'll have to lead your unit groups through strategic actions to defeat your opponents. The victory condition is simple: defeat all of your opponents' units.

The game features open dynamics. During the match, you can see your opponents' group information at all times. You can analyze in detail the hit probability and maximum damage you can inflict before engaging in combat with other groups. Therefore, much of the strategy is based on discrete actions and effectively utilizing your groups and abilities.

There are two basic game mechanics around which the match unfolds: engaging opposing groups and the guard formation. When you move your unit groups near opposing groups (one hexagon away), both groups enter in an engaged state. Groups in an engaged state cannot easily flee and cannot use abilities. However, positioning groups close to each other will give you combat bonuses against nearby opposing groups. On the other hand, the guard formation puts the group into watch mode. A group in watch mode will automatically attack any group that crosses its line of sight. As you can see, both mechanics counteract each other, and most of the abilities and resources you have during the match are based on supporting or countering these mechanics.

We hope you enjoy the Tabletop Fantasy War demo experience, and we appreciate all kinds of feedback and suggestions. For the final version of the game, there will be different game modes and maps for multiplayer, and an entirely new single-player mode to play a campaign and discover the mysteries of the fantasy world of Korsak.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
  • OS *: Windows 7 (SP1+), Windows 10 and Windows 11
  • Processor: x64 architecture with SSE2 instruction set support.
  • Memory: 4 MB RAM
  • Graphics: DX10, DX11, DX12 capable.
  • Storage: 200 MB available space
  • VR Support: No
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
  • OS *: Windows 7 (SP1+), Windows 10 and Windows 11
  • Processor: x64 architecture with SSE2 instruction set support.
  • Memory: 8 MB RAM
  • Graphics: DX10, DX11, DX12 capable.
  • Storage: 200 MB available space
  • VR Support: No

short_description: Tabletop Fantasy War is a turn-based strategy game where you create and customize your unit groups, deploy them on the battlefield, and command them with strategic actions. Your units are all you have. Every decision matters. Lead them wisely and defeat your opponents!
